title: Corner lot subdivision: reduced setback to the original secondary street
text: C3.3.2 Notwithstanding C3.3.1, the following reductions are permitted: iii. in areas coded R15 or higher, the street setback, may be reduced to 2.5m, or 1.5m to a porch, balcony, verandah or the equivalent, where a single house results from a subdivision of an original corner lot and has its frontage to the original secondary street.

replaces.note: only limb (b) carried; grouped dwelling with main frontage to a secondary street (a) and grouped dwelling fronting a communal street, ROW or shared access way (c) dropped

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

notes: Chapter 3 repeats the Chapter 2 wording: the concession applies 'where a single house results from a subdivision of an original corner lot' (p31), so as printed it does not reach a grouped dwelling; likely a carry-over (register ch3-050). Encoded unchanged; verify whether a grouped dwelling on such a lot qualifies. The original secondary street is the lot's primary street after subdivision, so the primary street setback fact is tested. The porch limb (1.5 m) is C3.3.2(iii)-r1.

verified.note: Wording confirmed on p31: the grouped dwellings chapter still says 'where a single house results from a subdivision of an original corner lot'. The page does not say whether a grouped dwelling qualifies.
